line: [Intro]
vault_lines: What do I mean? Let me break it down for you real quick
meaning:
The intro features a laid back, minimalist tropical house vibe, featuring simple piano chords and a ticking clock.

Tying into the line “You’re running out of time,” the clock is ticking slightly too fast (124 ticks per minute). This subtly reinforces the feeling that the singer is losing patience with his indecisive lover.



Furthermore, the pendulum and its continuous  swinging from the left to the right represents the girl’s indecisiveness Justin sings about.

line: You’re overprotective when I’m leavin’
vault_lines: What do I mean? Let me break it down for you real quick
meaning:
Despite Justin’s claim that the song is a generic commentary about women, many believe that this verse was directed at his former lover, Selena Gomez. This rumor became rampant when stills from the video showed Selena’s name.



Justin may have confirmed this theory in a November 2015 interview with Ellen DeGeneres. Entertainment Weekly reported it in this way:

In the first bit, she asked Bieber which — if any — new songs were about former girlfriend Selena Gomez.  “If there were [songs about Gomez], which three would they be?” she asked Bieber. He hesitated, so DeGeneres helped him fill in the blanks: “‘What Do You Mean?‘” DeGeneres said. “‘Sorry,’ a little bit,” he said in return, “and ‘Mark My Words.'”

Selena infamously made a list of rules for their relationship, including that Justin couldn’t hang out with other girls alone (overprotective when I’m leaving).

In early 2015, Selena posted a video of herself covering Drake’s “Preach” (you keep preaching).

Many believed that there was more to come with the Selena relationship. After all, “The Heart Wants What it Wants.” On October 17th 2015, these suspicions were heightened by the release of “Strong.”

However,  rumors of a possible comeback of Jelena ended in November 2018 when Bieber married model Hailey Baldwin.

line: You’re so indecisive of what I’m sayin’ Tryna catch the beat, make up your heart Don’t know if you’re happy or complainin’ Don’t want for us to end, where do I start?
vault_lines: What do I mean? Let me break it down for you real quick
meaning:
Justin’s lack of understanding is not due to a lack of effort. He compares it to trying to dance to the rhythm of her heartbeat, but it seems like the beat is constantly changing.

“Make up your heart” is also a play on the phrase “make up your mind,” but Justin implies that her emotions are at the core of her indecision.

Note the juxtaposition of “end” and “start” and how Justin uses it again (the other way round) in the second verse.

line: First you wanna go to the left, then you wanna turn right (Right) Wanna argue all day, makin’ love all night (All night) First you’re up, then you’re down, and then between (’Tween) Oh, I really wanna know
vault_lines: But I tell you to go
meaning:
Note the contrast of left, right, up, down, and between. While left/right and up/down are simple pairs, “between” describes a more complex situation. Her emotions are fighting each other and it’s causing her to have contradictory standpoints.

The lyrics are reminiscent of Katy Perry’s 2008 hit “Hot N Cold.”

You’re up and you’re down
You’re wrong when it’s right
It’s black and it’s white
We fight, we break up
We kiss, we make up

vault_lines: When I nod my head yes
meaning:
Justin is frustrated and confused by a girl who seems to not know what she wants.

This is not the first time Justin has touched on this subject. On Sean Kingston’s 2010 track “Eenie Meenie,” Bieber boldly addressed an indecisive lover:

Can’t make up your mind, mind, mind, mind, mind
Please don’t waste my time, time, time, time, time

https://youtu.be/prmmCg5bKxA?t=101

Actress/feminist activist Lena Dunham tweeted a protest to these lyrics, inferring that the line “When you nod your head yes but you wanna say no” contributed to rape culture, similar to the accusations against “Blurred Lines.” Of course, it’s entirely possible that she “nods her head yes” due to his fame; normally, she would say no to a relationship, but she does it for the Biebs, resulting in an unhealthy one-sided relationship.

line: FBI raided my house and shit was gettin’ dicey I was doin’ stupid shit to get people to like me
vault_lines: FBI raided my house and shit was gettin' dicey
meaning:
In 2014, Justin’s Calabasas home was raided by the police after he was accused of egging his neighbor’s house.

Lil Twist, who lived in Bieber’s mansion at the time, was arrested for possession of cocaine. He has since spoken out against Bieber’s management, claiming that they had him take the fall for Justin’s drug charges.



Whilst there is no evidence to distinguish whether these claims are true or not, Justin no longer associates with Twist and has been able to rehabilitate both his public image and his drug addiction.

The use of “sugar” and “pill” should be noted, as sugar pills are common placebos—"fake" treatments that seem real, but have no direct effect on the underlying medical issue. Justin’s lover is like a placebo; although she doesn’t give him what he needs in the relationship, he’s still infatuated by the thought of her.

line: You are to me A part of me just like anatomy

meaning:
Anatomy is the bodily structure of an organism—the overall composition of all of the essential parts that make the subject whole.

By declaring that his lover is metaphorically a part of his anatomy, Justin suggests that she is a permanent fixture in his life—just as important as any organ, bone, or muscle.



This romantic notion of someone “being a part” of another is featured in many popular songs, including Beyoncé’s “Resentment” and Ja Rule’s “Put it On Me”:

For that you’ll forever be a, part of me
Mind body and soul ain’t no I in we (baby)

line: Am I in love with you? Am I in love with you? Or am I in love with the feeling? I’m trying to find the truth, trying to find the truth But sometimes the heart is deceiving Can’t get out of my head and I need you to save me If I am delusional then maybe I’m crazy In love with you, am I in love with you? Or am I in love with the feeling?
vault_lines: You are to me
meaning:
The feeling of love can be a double-edged sword, blinding some and causing them to mistake the elation of connecting with another as love. This can lead one to question their emotions—do they crave their lover, or the feeling they get from the love itself?

In an interview with Elle Magazine in September 2015, Justin said that love, in fact, is not a feeling:

Love is a choice. Love is not a feeling. People have made it seem in movies that it’s this fairy tale. That’s not what love is. You’re not gonna want to love your girl sometimes but you’re gonna choose to love her. That’s something in life that I had to figure out.

Finding love can occasionally feel impossible, and forching a relationship can be poisonous for both parties. As Justin says, while settling down might feel like the right thing, it doesn’t always end up being what one truly wants.

Throughout his musical career, Bieber has had runaway love, somebody to love, had someone love him like they do, love him, and love themselves.

He’s also wanted one less lonely girl, one life, and one time, but here, he wants one love; just somebody who can love both emotionally and physically.

This likely refers to Selena Gomez, his ex-girlfriend. The couple broke up just months after this album’s release. 8 For to one is given through the Spirit the utterance of wisdom, and to another the utterance of knowledge according to the same Spirit, 9 to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit, 10 to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the ability to distinguish between spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues. 11 All these are empowered by one and the same Spirit, who apportions to each one individually as he wills.

The Charismatic and Pentecostal denominations in Christianity strongly uphold this belief and urge Christians to pursue the gift of speaking in tongues.

line: [Bridge] What I get from my reflection Is a difference in perception? From what the world may see
vault_lines: What I get from my reflection
meaning:
The way people see Justin, is not the way he really is. He’s been in the industry for years, and ever since he got famous, he’s been getting hate and negative publicity. In his younger days, people wouldn’t take him seriously — hit records like “Baby” got him a lot of fans, but a lot of haters as well.

Justin became an easy target for the media, because he was a young kid who didn’t yet know how the music industry worked. They were essentially just trying to bring him down.

Things escalated in 2013 — he started doing things such as yelling at paparazzi in the UK and peeing in a bucket. From then on, people would talk about Bieber even more, calling him arrogant and cocky. It was ruining a kid with a lot of potential.



For years, people have been trying to create a bad image of Bieber, exaggerating what he does wrong rather than focusing on his good actions. Justin himself is aware of this image being created of him. He wants people to see his true colors and start judging him based on who he is instead of what they read about him.

line: Life is worth living Life is worth living, so live another day The meaning of forgiveness People make mistakes Only God can judge me Life is worth living again Another day Life is worth living again
vault_lines: Life is worth living, so live another day
meaning:
There’s a slight change in the chorus here.

Instead of “People make mistakes, doesn’t mean you have to give in,” he sings “only God can judge me.” This again refers to the strong faith Justin has in God.

All the rough things Justin has been through, have made him feel like it may not be worth it. Some people make fun of Justin for opening up about this, but it doesn’t influence him anymore. He is proud to be a Christian, even though he doesn’t agree with everything that goes with it.

I think that with Christians, they’ve left such a bad taste in people’s mouths. Just like, overly pushy with the subject, overly churchy and religious. (…) I think that people, as soon as they start hearing me saying I’m a Christian, they’re like, “Whoa Justin, back up, take a step back.” Also, I do not want to shove this down anyone’s throat.

He also says it’s important to be open minded and not everyone experiences religion in the same way. He is happy with what he gets out of it and feels like he’s found himself. Life is finally worth living again for Bieber.

He thought his relationship wouldn’t last, but God restored his hope.

He mentions faith more often in this song. Justin has been opening up about the strength he finds in God a lot lately. In an interview with Complex, he said:

My faith has brought me to a whole other level. I love talking about my faith. (…) I’m not religious. I, personally, love Jesus and that was my salvation. I want to share what I’m going through and what I’m feeling and I think it shouldn’t be ostracized. I think that everybody should get their chance to share what they’re doing or where their journey is headed, whether they’re straight or gay or what they believe in.

His reputation still isn’t very stable: people have been sceptic about Justin and his abilities since he got famous. Justin may be more accepted at the moment, because his new music applies to a lot of people, but he knows that any small mistake can change people’s opinions back to negative.

As much as he wants people to like him, it’s difficult to please everyone. Justin is working on a better version of himself and though it seems to be working, his own happiness is the most important.

The whole time, Scooter always made sure I was safe and made sure situations didn’t escalate. He’d fix every situation. It almost wasn’t good, because I’d be like, any time I wanna do something, Scooter is gonna take care of it. It backfired a few times.
— Justin in Complex Magazine.

vault_lines: Ended up on a crossroad
meaning:
The past couple of years haven’t been easy for Justin. From the moment he rolled into the music industry in 2009, people have been hating on him. In the first years of his career people didn’t take his music seriously and made fun of his looks. All the negativity had a strong influence on his behavior; Justin started rebelling and got into serious trouble.

The fact people had an opinion on everything he did, put him in a difficult position. He was aware that he had to change, but he didn’t know how. In these lines, he uses two metaphors to describe the feeling.

line: Life is worth living Life is worth living, so live another day The meaning of forgiveness People make mistakes, doesn’t mean you have to give in Life is worth living again
vault_lines: Life is worth living, so live another day
meaning:
It’s very clear which message Justin wants to deliver: the song is a note to anyone listening to it, but also to himself. It’s his story.

Justin has been through a rough period, mainly in 2013 and 2014. He got negative media attention for things he did, such as using drugs and getting arrested for drag racing under influence.

Luckily he managed to change things around, and is now trying to show people he’s only human. He opened up about this in an interview with Complex:

I wouldn’t take back anything. I wouldn’t do anything over again. I would do it all the same way. I’m not going to say I’m sorry for the things that I’ve done because I think that it allows me to tell a story.

Everyone messes up sometimes, but forgiving is the key. Justin hopes people will give him another chance and judge him based on his music from now on. He sees the positive side of life again. By sharing his story, he wants his fans to realize that even when things are difficult, you have to keep going.

Now, I went through my shit, I came out on the other side, and I’m going to show you it gets better.

People are eager to the donations and they want to  immediately offer and sacrifice items of theirs for God, using the metaphor “running” here.



For many Christian denominations, specifically those that believe that the bread and wine offered at the altar transform into Jesus Christ’s true body and blood, the altar is a place to encounter God. This is why Justin says he is running to the altar like a “track star,” a champion in the sport of track and field, a sport in running, since he is so eager to meet and spend time with God.

This may also be referencing Psalms 43:4:

to God, my joy and my delight.
I will praise you with the lyre,
O God, my God.

Interestingly, the next line refers to playing the lyre, a musical instrument, so this would be a fitting verse to interpolate into a song.

An altar is also used at a wedding (it’s the structure under which we commonly see the bride and groom affirm their love for one another and a priest pronounce them married). Justin could be talking about his rapid marriage to Hailey Baldwin; the two dated from 2015 to 2016, then reconciled in May of 2018 and got married within six months. line: Relationships over the phone Talkin’ to your significant other all night long
vault_lines: Relationships over the phone
meaning:
Online dating has come a long way since its early days and has gone through many phases. What started as a niche concept has evolved into one of the most popular ways to meet people worldwide. But at the end of the day, building a family or maintaining a truly healthy and strong relationship goes beyond screens.

While one can express emotion and love through a screen—via texts and calls—people still crave physical touch to feel love in a tangible way. Whether it’s cuddling a significant other, kissing, or experiencing physical intimacy, these aspects can’t truly be fulfilled through a screen.

This also applies to long-distance relationships, which can be tough. But unlike online-only relationships, you eventually get to see your significant other. It might seem like a long wait, but making the most of it—through calls and texting—can still strengthen your bond. Even without physical touch, it can still be love. And in the end, it’ll all be okay.

line: Know it hurts to see the truth in your face Circumstances bring you down to your knees

meaning:
I see the pain. I see the truth. The truth is you realize that I’m not that perfect guy. The truth is I am flawed, and the truth is you are here with me and you made a conscious decision to accept me, and that truth hurts. The truth always hurts. And those circumstances, they can bring you down, all the way. They can break you all the way down, because when you go through something and you think something is one way and it’s not, that can break you down. It breaks you down, definitely your self esteem goes first, and then that follows by your mental health, and then usually that right there will manifest in your physical.

For her to actually know I’m not this guy. I’m not the dream guy. This is gonna break you down because you are gorgeous, and I still hurt you, and that’s gonna lower your self-esteem, but I’m gonna try my hardest to help build your self-esteem back up. And the most important thing is, I apologize for being a man, because even to this day, I need counseling. I feel like a lot of people of color were raised to not seek counseling or get any type of psychiatric help or anything, because it’s looked upon as “You’re crazy,” but it’s not.

It t took me a long time to realize that I have questions. Why, if I really love you and I really don’t want to hurt you, why? Even after having a period of time where we’re amazing, why would I at one point decide I’m gonna do this, knowing that this could hurt somebody that I love the most, and that I wouldn’t be able to live without? Those are the questions that I can’t answer. So I apologize for being a man, because it’s way harder than what it seems. It just looks easy, because we can just throw clothes on. We’re definitely are a lot easier to manage as far as what we have to do, everything just by being men.

But the inside, the part how we’re wired, whoever wired us, these questions that I have of myself that I do feel like I can get some answers with counseling or a psychiatrist. I’m not ashamed of it. I’m not ashamed to say it, but definitely left me to say I apologize for being a man. It’s just way more difficult than what it appears to be. That part of it is the reality of it. The reality of it is I’m still learning, at this latter age of my life, I’m still learning and I’m still learning myself, let alone learning things around me. I’m still learning myself. And having questions for myself that I need to find answers to in order to be the best version of myself. I have to figure it out and wrap my hand around it.

It was a warning: Now it’s up to you to say, “You know what, I see what’s on the table, and I’m not okay with it, I’m gonna go and find another table.” Or, “I see what’s on the table, and I love you so much, I love you unconditionally, I’m here and I’m gonna ride it out, because I just fuck with you as a human, and I love your good and your bad.” That’s where this word “unconditional” becomes this thing, where it’s like, “Do you love the good and the bad of me? Or do you just love the good part?” It’s easy to love the good part. It’s always easy to love the part that’s the easy part to love. But then when you get to the part where I hurt you, or I made this decision, are you gonna leave or do you love, does that unconditional part cover that part too?

I think that her having an opportunity to leave for the last time, in my mind, it sounded like that place where she was. She made up her mind that she just was gonna love me unconditionally, no matter what it came along with. Still, all I ever wanted to do with anybody that I’ve ever loved was protect their feelings.

line: Should’ve been adjusted to my life
vault_lines: Should've been adjusted to my life
meaning:
It’s very selfish, but as humans we’re selfish beings, and even more so, you look back in the day, look at the lifestyle of humans and how we’ve evolved from having a normal average of 10 to 12 kids in a household, to now, it’s like no kids, or one kid, or two kids. That just comes from us as human beings realizing that all the programs and everything that was set up for us, it wasn’t really about us, it was a program that we fell into, and then we as humans are starting to be more selfish. I don’t think it was a bad thing, but you now look at me, take me for instance. I waited until I was 38 years old to have a baby, to even think about having a baby, because I wanted to live my life.

Back in the day, you weren’t really thinking about living your life. You were just thinking, “This is all we have; let’s just make a family.” You look up 12 kids later, on a farm, and then you’re old, but now it’s more about us. We’ve become these selfish beings, and it’s not saying that it’s bad or wrong, but that’s where we are. That line, “Should have been adjusted to my life,” it comes from a real place of you signed up to be with me, and you knew what you were signing up to, you knew what you were signing up for. I would think that after this amount of time, you would have adjusted, or removed yourself. It’s one or the other.

line: Sometimes it’s hard to face reality, oh, oh Even though you might get mad at me, oh, oh Sometimes it’s hard to face reality
vault_lines: Sometimes it's hard to face reality, oh, oh
meaning:
My reality is I’m just, I’m a father, I’m a husband, and the struggle of just being human, the struggle of being here is the reality of just waking up and dealing with the things that we all deal with. I feel like it’s just insecurities, and having to face those insecurities, and trying to figure out ways to go through life to be less insecure. It always seems like it’s about getting to a place of being confident, and being secure, so that you can make the best decisions and be the best version of yourself. I’m just still working on myself. I’m working to be the best husband. I’m working to be the best father. The reality of it is, is that it’s not easy, it’s something that there’s no real handbook or manual or blueprint of how to do this.

There are ways, there are methods that have worked for people, but everybody’s different in such a unique way that something that worked for that individual might not work for the next person. It’s literally going through life and figuring it out as you go, and you’re just hoping that the decisions that you make aren’t detrimental, and you’re hoping that they’re positive, that the reaction and the response from your decisions are great. These are all things that we go through every day. I know I go through them, teetering through life, hoping to just be the best that I could be. And I fell. I let myself down. I let people down, because being a human, we’re just not perfect. I think facing reality every day is so, I think this record connects and speaks to people because everybody’s reality is so different, but it’s there. They can’t get around it.

You can try to go around reality, but it’s gonna eventually hit you in your face. Eventually you might come around it this way, and it’s gonna hit you right there. I think that the lyric being so simple, sometimes it’s hard to face reality, even though you might be mad at me. Even being mad at me, I look at that as me being mad at myself, and just not making good decisions. But at the same time, learning from those decisions, and saying next time I’m gonna make a better decision, but I’m gonna deal with my reality right now.

line: Always rain the most in April Every scale needs to be stable Earth keeps spinnin’ around, we’re breathin’ So thankful
vault_lines: Always rain the most in April
meaning:
Justin is joining a long literary line of reflection on spring rain (there’s also the well-known proverb, “April showers bring May flowers”).

Back in the 1380s, Geoffrey Chaucer opens his Canterbury Tales:

Whan that Aprille with his shoures soote,
The droghte of March hath perced to the roote,

Some centuries later, T.S. Eliot would start his poem The Waste Land with these lines:

April is the cruellest month, breeding
Lilacs out of the dead land, mixing
Memory and desire, stirring
Dull roots with spring rain.

Like Justin, Chaucer and Eliot realized that the hardships of April rain could also make for a new start, however soggy.

line: Cry on my shoulder, I know your heart breaks, but Lay it all down, and I can love it away Just stay by my side, oh

meaning:
Justin wraps up his message of support with heartfelt empathy. I know your heart breaks acknowledges that he truly understands her hurt.

Lay it all down is an encouragement for her to unload all her sorrow and burdens onto him.

I can love it away is a beautiful expression, he believes that through his love, he can help dissolve her pain. This reflects Justin’s faith in the healing power of love. It’s almost like he views love as a balm or medicine that can mend a broken heart.

And finally, just stay by my side is both plea and reassurance: he wants her to remain with him, and he’s reminding her he’s right here next to her through everything. It also hints that he finds his purpose in being there for her; if she stays by him, he can do his job of loving her troubles away.

Notably, these lines come after a period earlier this year where rumors swirled about their marriage being in trouble; Hailey even had to publicly shut down breakup gossip. Justin declaring stay by my side and promising to love her pain away is a direct counter to those rumours: it’s him stating that they’re a team and he’s devoted to making it work through any heartache.

line: So cry on my shoulder, that lone melody
vault_lines: So cry on my shoulder, that lone melody

He repeats the invitation to cry on him, adding a poetic twist: that lone melody. This phrase likely describes the sound of her crying: a single, sad melody.

By calling it a melody, Justin is almost romanticising her vulnerability, implying there’s a lonely music in her tears that he hears and responds to. It shows how attuned he is to her pain, even finding a somber beauty in it because it’s real.

The word lone underscores that she might feel alone in her sorrow, but by telling her to cry on his shoulder, he’s ensuring she’s not alone.

The combination of emotional and musical imagery here emphasises how their love and comfort is almost lyrical in itself.

line: You better believe that I can hold all the weight That you feel inside
vault_lines: You better believe that I can hold all the weight
meaning:
The “weight… inside” refers to her heavy feelings: stress, sadness, fear… Justin urges her to truly trust (you better believe) that he is strong enough to carry her emotional burdens.

There’s also an undercurrent of proving himself: perhaps Justin knows there were times he fell short or wasn’t as present (like that Vogue cover incident where he reacted insensitively initially), and now he’s emphasizing that he can take on anything she’s going through. This line might address those who doubted his support, he’s affirming he’s emotionally capable and willing.

It’s touching because it frames love as partnership: her burdens are his burdens now. Justin is effectively echoing wedding vow sentiments, in sickness and in health, he’s there to carry the weight.

This is Justin telling Hailey that not every problem requires an immediate fix, nor will every tough time lead to a collapse.

Nothing needs to work out means they don’t have to have everything solved right now. It’s permission to let things be unresolved for a moment. Nothing needs to break reassures her that a rough patch or a bad day doesn’t mean their relationship (or her world) will fall apart.

This line speaks to people (like Hailey) who might put pressure on themselves to always be okay or to fix everything. Justin is easing that pressure.

There’s a subtext of patience and faith here: some things will resolve in time, and some situations don’t need drastic action (like breaking up or freaking out) just because things feel hard.

line: Like water to a flower, babe, I know you need the rain
vault_lines: Like water to a flower, babe, I know you need the rain

This beautiful metaphor reassures Hailey that it’s okay to cry or go through tough times. Just as a flower needs water (rain) to grow, a person sometimes needs to feel sadness or shed tears to heal and grow. Justin is telling her that her tears or down moments are natural and even necessary.

By saying I know you need the rain, he’s showing that he understands her deeply, he knows that she can’t always be strong and sunny, and that letting out emotions (the rain) will ultimately nourish her spirit (the flower).

This line flips a common perspective: rather than seeing tears as something negative, he frames them as something positive and nurturing. It’s a tender way to encourage her not to hold back her feelings.

It gets hard to face means life becomes difficult to deal with. This could refer to the pressure of media scrutiny or personal struggles with self-doubt and mental health.

We know Hailey has had challenging moments (like intense public scrutiny, or any personal insecurities), so Justin is acknowledging those periods when her bright, confident exterior (sunlight) is overtaken by doubt or pain (shadows). meaning:
“Living water” refers to God–this metaphor is used a few times in the Bible. For instance, in Jeremiah 17:13, the prophet speaks against people who forsake God and goes on to say:

Lord, you are the hope of Israel; all who forsake you will be put to shame. Those who turn aside from you will be written in the dust, because they have forsaken the Lord, the spring of living water.

Jeremiah describes God as “the spring of living water.” When Bieber sings this line, he uses the same comparison to say that everyone is searching for God and proof that He exists.



God is the "spring of living water"



[Credit: BibleProject]

The concept of living water is also presented in John 4:13-14, where Jesus alludes to God’s living water while speaking to a Samaritan woman. He says:

13Everyone who drinks this [normal] water will be thirsty again, 14but whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give them will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life.

The “spring” of water that Jesus states he will provide is God’s spring. Jesus' and Jeremiahs' words are connected; Jeremiah also refers to God as a “spring of living water.”

After Jesus says this, the Samaritan woman tells Jesus to give her this “living water.” Bieber sings that people are searching for living water, similar to this Samaritan woman; people want to receive eternal life from God.

The living water that people search for comes from God, and as Jesus states in the above verse, those who drink the water from God and not forsake him will “never be thirsty again” and more importantly, receive eternal life.

meaning:
“So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.”  1 Corinthians 10:31

So, as we know, “Hallelujah” means “Praise God.”

In this song, Justin Bieber connects the ordinary elements of his daily life – the simple moments of his day and routine – with the desire to use those moments to, first, glorify God, and second, thank God. These two things are inseparably connected: gratitude and praise flow into one another, and one naturally gives birth to the other.

We see a beautiful example of Justin Bieber trying to find, within his everyday life, reasons to praise, glorify, and thank God, just as it is written in 1 Corinthians.

This is a powerful song for worship and contemplation – an invitation to recognize God’s care and presence in the simple details of our own lives. Justin Bieber has walked through a difficult and deeply personal spiritual journey, moving from the challenges of fame toward a search for Christ. This particular song carries a beautiful simplicity while also holding significant theological depth.

Bieber makes a slight variation of the well-known idiom “absence makes the heart grow fonder”, which explains how two people become more affectionate, after being apart for a period of time.

In historical contexts, the phrase originated from Sextus Properitus, a poet from the Roman times; he first mentioned it within his book named Elegies:

Always toward absent lovers love’s tide stronger flows

Its use in the song can be seen as quite relevant to Justin and Hailey’s relationship timeline. From what began as a friendship became a little fling in 2015, due to which JB’s tour, past relationship drama with singer and actress Selena Gomez, and speculations surrounding “non-exclusivity”, led to a break-up.



(pictured): Throwback to Bieber and Baldwin looking particularly cozy in an old Instagram picture posted on her page

Notably, Bieber shared an interview with Beats 1 host, Zane Lowe, where–as well as becoming candid about his dark past, health conditions, and album release–he explained how he realised that Hailey was “the one”:

I’d seen [Hailey] at an event. I’d seen her with a baby and something just clicked. line: Every heartbreak has its season It ain’t always summer in June
vault_lines: Every heartbreak has its season
meaning:
This is a reference to how Summer/Spring months are generally believed to be the “uncuffing season” as opposed to the colder months that are the “cuffing season.” Generally, this happens as people tend to form relationships in the winter due to the colder and lonelier nature to be “boo’d up”. On the other hand, breaking up happens in spring/summer so the individuals can be “free” and not tied down for the summer.

Psychologist, Dr Danielle Forshee elaborated that cuffing season occurs because:

There’s a decrease in sunlight, and the body is producing more melatonin, a hormone that responds to darkness and makes you tired, and producing less serotonin, the neurotransmitter that makes us feel happy and good.

On the other hand, she also elaborated on “uncuffing season”

As the sunlight comes out more, the brain produces less melatonin and more serotonin, making you feel happier, you may not feel such a need to be around someone else to provide that sense of security and happiness.

Also, summer and spring are classically related to a time of mating and more activity. Longer days, with more daylight, provide feelings of happiness and steadiness.

With “It ain’t always summer in June”, it’s shown that not everything in the summer is enjoyment, as even breakups can turn a “pleasurable” season into bitterness – it loosely signifies that there isn’t always happiness, even if it’s summer.

Later, “And it look like winter for you” alludes to the depression and sadness (commonly associated with short winter days) that people go through during a breakup.

line: [Produced by Skrillex]
vault_lines: What about the children?
meaning:
Skrillex has worked on numerous tracks (with and without supporting producers like BLOOD) on Bieber’s LP, such as the two massive singles “I’ll Show You”, and “Sorry”. He’s also produced other tracks, as well, such as The Feeling (with Ian Kirkpatrick), Where are U Now (with Diplo), Hit the Ground and more.

This track is very much a “banger” electronic track, opening with a pulsating synth bassline, accompanied by some very rapid flute melodies, eventually dropping with a high pitched, squeaky, synth, being accompanied by a major lazer style, soft bass melody. The back end of the track receives some very solid flute notes, adding to the overall massiveness to the track, despite the relatively small variety of instrumentation.

Skrillex talked about the track on NME as well:

“The original version of ‘Children’ was written like a typical EDM song at the writing session we did. It almost sounded like something that Swedish House Mafia could’ve produced a couple of years ago. I don’t mean that in a negative way. It was major sounding too, so I reproduced it to be minor sounding and emotional. It’s a very simple message Justin is conveying through that song. I can’t speak for him, but I think he’s starting to grapple with the fact he’s a role model for a generation.”

line: [Verse 3: Justin Bieber]
vault_lines: If I'm not butt naked, I'm in my drawers
meaning:
Taken from BOYDERCAM youtube account:

“At the time, it was just an inside joke—a "just for fun” remix to a song between some friends killing time. Even to this day, I never intended to
release it. But, five years and 50 million fans later, it’s proven hard to keep these types of things in the vault. We’ve had ample opportunity to do put it out ourselves, but the fact that this song remained unreleased until now should be indicative of the fact that it was never intended to be heard by anyone other than those of us who were goofing around in the recording studio that day. Nevertheless, here’s your opportunity to relive that moment and laugh along with us.

The story for this particular song is as follows: Brain Bangley and I were in our basement in Atlanta, GA recording when Justin Bieber’s Mom dropped him off. The honest truth is that we didn’t initially let him record with us—we knew Scooter and his mom wouldn’t be cool with him “rapping” in general (especially considering what typical rap content entails).

Recording was just a hobby at the time—instead of shooting hoops, we make stupid rap songs. We wanted Justin to stay upstairs and play MarioKart, but he insisted and persisted. So we gave him a notepad and paper, sent him upstairs, and said, “If you can write 16 bars, we’ll let you hop on.”

About 10 minutes later, Brain Bangley and I were a few lines into our verses when, through the makeshift blanket doors of the studio, we heard
an excited, high-pitch voice exclaim, “I’m done!” That he was. I thought it was clever and fun, so we decided to let him record it, all the while thinking we could just delete it so Scooter would never hear. We sent him into the studio, and he laid down his verse in one take. We laughed, high-fived, went upstairs and played video games. That was it.

*** Also, a personal note from me: keep in mind that Justin was just a regular kid. He still is. We all are. We all have different journeys. We all have a life we need to experience in order to grow and mature. I always wonder how beautiful the world could be if more people took the energy they directed at the faults of celebrity figures and diverted it towards their own issues.

In this world, relationships are all we ever really have. Relationships with certain amazing people in our lives are what make us who we are. The
reason the best songs, movies and moments are made. They’re the reason I’m writing this. I truly hope that Justin will find true love and friendship in his life. I’m not saying that their aren’t amazing people in Justin’s life, because there are and I know them personally. I’m just saying that it might make his world a little less confusing at times. Maybe instead of ridiculing him, next time just appreciate the fact that you have authentic people in your world. People that won’t secretly sell your image, or a song you created five years ago, to an online publication for next month’s
rent money.

We were fortunate to get to know Justin during his last year of being a “regular” person. He became a younger brother to all of us. I understood Justin as a wide-eyed, big-hearted, eternally curious, regular person with extraordinary talents. And trust me, he is still that person.

I still believe in the big hearted Justin Bieber I knew five years ago in Atlanta, GA, the same way I believe in any of my friends whenever they hit a rough patch in their life—be it televised or lived out privately.

Have a beautiful day.

Love,
Boyder"
